title: First-order structures: assignments, satisfaction, and truth

based_on.title: Model Theory for Algebra and Algebraic Geometry

summary: Interpret first-order symbols in nonempty structures, evaluate formulas, and prove free-variable, substitution, and isomorphism invariance.
abstract: Every natural number has a larger natural number, but the two-element order has a largest element. The same first-order sentence can therefore be true in one structure and false in another. A structure gives meanings to the language's symbols, and an assignment supplies values for free variables. Recursive evaluation shows that only the free variables appearing in a formula affect its truth, that substituting a term agrees with assigning its value, and that a bijection preserving all the interpreted symbols preserves every sentence. A theory then describes the structures in which all its sentences hold.
